newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Iran's Velayati urges Afghan peace talks.
newsitem.headline: Iran's Velayati urges Afghan peace talks.

text.p: Iranian Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati said on Wednesday that the crisis in Afghanistan could not be resolved militarily and all factions should negotiate a peaceful settlement.

"We believe that (the) Afghanistan problem doesn't have a military solution," Velayati told reporters in the Kazakh capital Almaty after talks with Kazakh President Nursultan Nazarbayev. "All factions should sit down together, talk together to reach a peaceful settlement in Afghanistan."

Velayati is on a lightning tour of the former Soviet republics of Central Asia to discuss events in neighbouring Afghanistan, where government forces are battling the radical Islamic Taleban militia who drove them out of the capital late last month.
Velayati said Iran would not intervene in Afghanistan but accused other unnamed states of provoking the situation inside the mountainous country torn apart by years of bloody civil war.

"We don't want to intervene in the internal affairs of Afghanistan or any other countries," Velayati said, but added: "The intervention of other countries in the internal affairs of Afghanistan is the main original problem and the main victims in this process are the people of Afghanistan."

Iran recognises the ousted government of President Burhanuddin Rabbani. Iranian media have accused the United States, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan of backing the Taleban. Earlier on Wednesday, the official Iranian news agency IRNA reported that all but one of Iran's diplomats had been withdrawn from Kabul.
